## DONE — what this phase actually completed, with the evidence

 **1 · A PERSON'S PICK FOR A CLOSE MATCH. Built real, switched off.** A REVIEW-band match — close to the client's typed address, not close enough for us to choose it — was FAILED, code `MATCH_REVIEW`, and kept nothing. The S10 spec (A.2 step 4, A.8 point 7) always said what should happen instead: the ranked list goes to a person and nothing is written until they resolve it. There was nowhere to send it.

-  `src/connectors/matching.ts` gained `MatchResult.ranked` — every scored candidate, best first, **in memory only**, exactly as `top` already was — and `applyPick`, which offers that list **in the REVIEW band and in no other**: an ACCEPT is already decided, a REJECT is a choice between wrong answers, and a `chosen` key handed in outside the band is ignored. A choice names a **record** (a certificate number, a location id, a transaction id, a company number, a UPRN) and never a position in a list, so a list that came back in a different order cannot move a choice onto another building.

-  All six connectors that score candidates now offer their own list and take a choice: `epc.ts`, `cqc.ts`, `price-paid.ts`, `planning.ts`, `companies-house.ts`, `homedata.ts`. Planning applies it **per service**, so a choice made from planning.data.gov.uk's list is never looked for in PlanIt's.

-  `src/web/match-review.ts` is the back office half. Its own switch, `PICK_SWITCHES.MATCH_REVIEW_PICK`, **false** — a third map beside `REGISTER_SWITCHES` and `CLAUDE_SWITCHES`, because what it turns on is not a connector but a screen showing one client's staff a handful of other buildings' entries, which is a different decision with a different owner. `connectorSwitchReadings` reads it, so a claim's stamp says whether a figure on it could have been a person's pick.

-  **AFTER A SIGNED ENGAGEMENT ONLY, AND WHATEVER THE SOURCE'S TIER** — asserted server-side against the signature record through `assertSignedEngagement`, the same function and the same record as the paid tier's. Safeguard S15 rules out showing a prospect other buildings' records. **Which lookup may be picked from is read from ****`research_sources`****, never from the request**, exactly as `retryFailedSource` decides what may be retried.

-  **The list is fetched again for the request that shows it and is never stored, logged or shown to a client** (A.8 point 8, condition CA5). There is no candidate table and no cache. Showing the list stores nothing at all and does not even rewrite the source's row.

-  **Only the chosen record is stored, through ****`ingestRegisterRecord`** — the one door, where N2 is checked — called by `storeResearchOutcomes` exactly as an ordinary click calls it, **at grade B at most**, derived rather than typed: `worstGrade([the source's own max_grade, UNMEASURED_MATCH_GRADE_CAP])`.

-  **The choice, who made it and the score go on the audit chain**, kind `REGISTER_MATCH_PICKED`, with the grade and whether anything was stored, and **never the candidate or its label** — that is the register's own address line. `register_match_picks` (migration 042) holds where the decision landed; the chain holds every one of them in order.

-  **Choosing NONE is an answer and is kept.** It writes a pick row with no key, an audit row and a source row that says a person looked, and it keeps no fact: every question stays asked (N4).

-  **A choice the register no longer offers keeps NOTHING** and says to look at the list again. Falling back to the nearest one would be the auto-selection A.2 step 4 forbids.

-  Two POST routes (`.../research/pick`, `.../research/pick/choose`) and a "Choose which one it is" button drawn only where the lookup itself recorded REVIEW, the letter is signed and the switch is on. **Showing the list is a POST on purpose**: it is a call outside, an audit row and, on a paid lookup, money — a GET that did all three is a page a crawler or a back button could spend money on.

 **2 · THE ENERGY CERTIFICATE'S DOMESTIC CODES, DECODED OR NOT KEPT.** A domestic certificate gives the construction age band as a letter on each `sap_building_parts[]` entry ("M") and the tenure as a number at the top (1). `epc.ts` kept neither, and said so. It now reads the register's own code lists — `GET /api/codes` and `GET /api/codes/info?code=&key=&schemaVersion=`, read on 23 September 2026 and recorded in `SUPPLIER_DOCS` with what they answer and what they do **not** say. The **main** building part's band is the building's band (the first entry), and the certificate's own `schema_type` is the version asked for, because the same letter means different things under different schemas. **A code that could not be decoded is not kept in any form** — not the letter, not a guess, not a value returned for another schema version — and the words say the question stays asked. Neither call is made for a non-domestic or display certificate, which carries neither code. Found and fixed in the same function: a `dwelling_type` written as `{value, language}` rather than a string (RdSAP-Schema-19.0 writes one) was silently losing the building type.

 **3 · THE LAND REGISTRY'S WORDS WITH THE ENGINE'S SENTENCE.** `CB_REGISTRY.derive()` puts "Our records show you paid {v} for this property" into `provenance.price_paid.confirm`. The records are HM Land Registry's Price Paid Data, whose Open Government Licence **prescribes** the credit and says it must appear verbatim, **2021 included** — and the provenance carried none. `HMLR_PPD_ATTRIBUTION` is now a named constant in the layer, carried on `price_paid` and `completion_date` and on **no other field**: `tenure` is on the same source in that map and at the address question is the title register's answer, so a credit there would be a false statement of origin. Every other derived field carries `attribution: null` rather than nothing, so a reader testing for it gets an answer either way. The extractor was re-run and four assertions were added to suite O, in both engine modes; **all four go red on ****`Caprebate site.html.bak-phase146h`**** through the redirect hook** (1248 pass / 4 fail against the pre-change copy). The first draft of the first assertion compared the module to itself and passed on the old copy — the red run is what found it, and the words are now written out in the harness rather than read from the thing being tested.

 **What was re-derived, not inherited (step 8).** Site harness **1252 pass / 0 fail / 4 xfail**, the same with `--package`; phase3 **413**; phase9 **397**; back end **1355 pass across 69 files** for the whole `npm run check`; **3,417** in all. The drift checker found seven lines asserting the old figures in the present tense and all seven were corrected. The CRM fold check went red on twenty-seven §4 line references my own edits had moved and on the two new routes it could not find described; both are fixed and it is GREEN, self-test included. The register check, the plain-words check (and `--self-test`), the notices, brand and analytics checks, the extraction verifier, `extract --check` and `payload-proof` are all green.

 **Documents pushed to the board.** `CAPREBATE-DEVELOPER-SPEC.md`, `Build-Prep-06-Developer-Build-Specification-v2.md` and `Caprebate-Decided-And-Not-Decided-v1.md` were re-uploaded to item 12937209644 and the Files column read back: eight files, no duplicates, and each one's MD5 compared against its upload ETag. The Developer Spec's one page gains a **fourth precondition** — the pick's switch, which has no account and no key and is the data protection officer's.

## PHASE 146i — the document reader's follow-ons: the two fields a person must vouch for, and a screen that says what happened when a reading fails (23 September 2026, Mac copy)

 **Model: Opus. Ran and closed 23 September 2026 on the Mac copy, after Phase 146h.** Board item 13115053060. Commit on `main` at github.com/ldhillonaqlios/caprebate. **The rules for every integration phase held: built real and switched off, no key in the tree, every test on recorded answers with no network, the two gates and N4 unchanged. ****`CLAUDE_SWITCHES.DOCUMENT_READING`**** is still ****`false`**** and this phase did not touch it.**

### DONE

 **1 · THE TWO FIELDS NOBODY COULD VOUCH FOR — and the reason it mattered is not the one the prompt leads with.** `assertClaimsWritable` (04-phase-work/phase3/caprebate-client-doc-ingestion.ts) keeps `grant_funder_name` and `brc_issuing_body` only on the footing that the value names an ORGANISATION, and `UploadReading.discriminants` defaulted to `{}` because nothing ever set it. The refusal is for the WHOLE set of claims, so a grant funding agreement and a building regulations completion certificate kept **nothing at all** — two document types that could never be captured. **The ingestion module was not changed**, because its refusal is right where it sits; the fix is that an unvouched field never reaches it.

-  **`src/web/document-reading.ts`**** (new).** The two fields, the question each one asks in words, the three answers, what a recorded answer tells `assertClaimsWritable`, and the record of what a reading did. The answer is kept against the LOGICAL document, not one upload of it. **Only ****`yes`**** keeps a field**: `no`, `not sure` and no row at all are one decision (N4). The row still exists for a `no` or a `not sure`, so "somebody looked and was not sure" can be told from "nobody has been asked".

-  **`readAndClaim`**** (src/web/uploads.ts)** reads the person's answer and takes an unvouched field OUT of the extraction before the claims are built. The outcome carries `left_out` and says in plain words what came out and why. The field that came out is still ASKED of the client.

-  **The page and who may answer.** `vouchDocumentField` in src/web/documents.ts authorises it (`document.vouch` — Admin and Sales; a write, so the view-only login is refused, and never the client, who would be vouching for their own document) and audits it as `DOCUMENT_FIELD_VOUCHED` with the field, the answer and what it replaced — **never the value**. Three buttons, no script, one form.

-  **Migration 043** adds `document_field_vouches`. No name is stored in it.

 **2 · WHEN A READING DOES NOT WORK, A SCREEN SAYS SO.** `finishUpload` has returned a `ReadingOutcome` with a reason in plain words since Phase 146g and nothing drew it, so a document that came back unreadable looked exactly like one nobody had asked about. One `document_readings` row per reading (migration 043), drawn on the STAFF document page in words with its reason, newest first, per version. **No row is written where the reader was not wired in or where the switch is off** — with the switch off a finished upload must behave exactly as it did before Phase 146g, and a row is a difference. The empty case is drawn too, because "we have not tried" and "we tried and could not" are different facts and a blank space says neither. The client sees neither this nor the question.

 **3 · AND THAT IS WHEN THE PLAIN-WORDS CHECK CHANGED — point 6 of Phase 146g's prompt, which came due today.** `src/connectors/claude.ts` is now on the check's EXTRA list, because its reasons reach a screen at last. Its two **model instructions** are exempt **BY NAME** (`EXTRACTION_SYSTEM`, `PAGES_SYSTEM`) through a new `EXEMPT_CONSTS` map keyed on the file, not by their opening words — so a plainer sentence elsewhere in that file is still read, a renamed constant loses its exemption rather than keeping it by accident, and the same constant name in another file is not exempt at all. Four new self-test cases hold each of those four properties.

 **THE TESTS, AND THEY WERE PROVED TO FAIL.** `test/phase146i.test.ts` — twenty-two tests on recorded answers, no key and no network, every document invented. **Sixteen of the twenty-two go RED** when `uploads.ts` or `documents.ts` is swapped for its `.bak-phase146i` copy (ten and eleven respectively, overlapping); the six that stay green are the ones holding the control that was already right. One of them is the defect itself, stated precisely: `assertClaimsWritable` on an unvouched field **together with a perfectly good one** refuses both, and the good one on its own was always writable — which is exactly what this phase gets back.

 **THE CHECKS, ALL RUN ON THE MAC COPY AT THE CLOSE.** `npm run check` exit 0 — lint-sql green, typecheck 0 errors, **1377 pass / 0 fail across 70 files**. Site harness **1252 pass / 0 fail / 4 xfail**, identical in both modes. `verify-extraction` 0, `extract --check` 0. phase3 **413**, phase9 **397**, both from inside their folders. Drift checker exit 0, `--self-test` 0, negative control exit 1 as it must. Plain-words check GREEN and `--self-test` clean. CRM fold check GREEN. Register check exit 0 on a refreshed snapshot. `payload-proof` PASS. **Project total, re-derived and not inherited: 3,439 passing assertions.**

 **THE PAPERWORK.** The Developer Spec gained the new route, row 5 gained both follow-ons, its harness figures were re-derived, and **ten stale §4 line references were corrected** — the fold check found every one of them, and they were stale because this phase's own edits moved the lines. `README-file-index.md` gained a Phase 146i section. `src/app.ts`'s `STUBS` row for the document reader says what this phase built. Entry **SDP-P39** was added to FOR THE SOLICITOR, THE DPO AND THE DEVELOPER with the register's own counts restated (seventy-four entries covering sixty-five board items; 119 items at "Built — awaiting sign-off", forty-five / nine / sixty-five, counted in code). **Word question 210** was added to the data protection officer's section of the Word questions document, which now holds 210 Heading 2 paragraphs.

## Every other check, and every negative control, with its exit code read on its own line

 Green where it must be: the extraction verifier (21 checks, 24 switches all false, the free-register gate shut), `extract --check`, the notices acceptance check (24 structural checks pass, 9 need the host and were NOT run, 7 facts unset), the CRM fold check and its self-test, the sign-off register check and its self-test, the drift checker and its self-test and its stray-copy guard, the brand check and its self-test, the plain-words check and its self-test, the analytics allow-list check and its self-test, the surveyor payload proof, the gated-exit renderer proof, the cash-route proof and its self-test, and the matching measurement tool's self-test.

 Red where it must be, each run on its own line so the exit code is the check's own: the drift checker against four invented figures exits 1 and lists eleven; given three figures it exits 2 and refuses, which is not a failure report; the plain-words check against the pre-change copies exits 1; the gated-exit proof against the copy from before the repair exits 1 and five of ten checks fail; the cash-route proof against the copy from before the window work exits 1 and exactly the three expected checks fail; the matching measurement tool's live run exits 2 and refuses, because the data protection officer has not answered.

 **The payload proof passed on both halves**, which is the half that matters: a surveyor's captured response carries none of the sealed estimate's seven fields on any route it can reach, and an administrator's carries all seven on every route that holds them.

 **A control that did not run as written, found in this sweep's own working and recorded because it is the exact shape the sweep hunts.** The first pass at the negative controls put each command in a shell loop that split on a vertical bar, and in this shell that produced `node` with no arguments — which exits 1. Five controls "passed" without running, and one that should exit 2 reported 1. Re-run one per line, every exit code was right. A pipe into `tail` has the same effect the other way: it hands back `tail`'s exit code, which is always 0. **That is now written into COORDINATES beside the checks, not into a note beneath it.**

## What the sweep found

### 1. Lakhbir changed the business's email domain in a copy of a document on his Desktop, and nothing in the project has seen it

 There are two copies of the accounts-and-keys setup guide. The one in the project folder was written by the build on 22 September at 15:32 and has never been opened — revision 1, last saved by nobody. The one on the Desktop is revision 2, **last saved by Lakhbir Dhillon on 22 September at 19:47**, and differs in exactly two lines, both in the box of facts an account application asks for: the business email changed from contactus@caprebate.com to **contactus@caprebate.co.uk**, and the website from caprebate.com to **caprebate.co.uk**.

 The project has never heard it. **contactus@caprebate.com**** appears 196 times** across the tree — in the engagement letter, the privacy notice, the public notices page, the complaint form and the sending address the back office uses — and caprebate.co.uk appears in none of them as an address we use. The live task for creating the mailbox names the .com address. Create it and the whole build is on .com for good.

 Both domains were registered on the same day and both work: checked by DNS on 23 September, they answer with the same web address, the same mail servers, the same nameservers and the same sender policy. A domain we do not own returns nothing, which is the control. So nothing forces the answer. **And nobody ever chose .com**: it arrived when a phase tidying a wireframe on 31 August changed 77 lines from .co.uk to .com and every later document copied it. Written up as question 211 in the Word questions document, and the mailbox task now carries the finding in full so nobody creates the wrong address.

### 2. "There is still no task for the CIBSE terms" — written on 12 September, still true eleven days and three sweeps later

 The task about mapping equipment lives ends its comment of 12 September with that sentence. Searched on 23 September: no board item named CIBSE, no question in either questions document, and no mention anywhere outside the cost model's own code and tests. Ageing plant element by element needs two tables on two licences — the government valuation office's obsolescence scales, which are tracked, and CIBSE's plant lives, which were tracked nowhere. The model carries the CIBSE table by name, empty, and the completeness gate refuses all 103 elements of the fixture taxonomy because not one has a life. **Clearing the valuation office licence alone unlocks nothing.** A board item now exists and the reading is written into a phase.

### 3. A cost the engine still spends before a signature it can no longer be spent before

 The job economics module's section 6 says, in the present tense, that the paid address lookup "is the only per-claim cost incurred before a client signs anything", and that "an enquirer with eleven care homes who never signs costs us eleven lookups and returns nothing". Lakhbir's rule of 4 September makes both impossible, and the connector built on 23 September is gated on a signed engagement and an operator's click. **The same file says so two hundred lines above** — a note added on 17 September that diagnoses the staleness and does not fix it. The function is still named for a pre-signature cost, its refusal text still repeats both sentences, and when a price is supplied it divides by the conversion rate to charge the lookup to enquiries that failed, producing a figure four times the truth. Two "at a high price" branches and a question recorded as open rest on the same dead premise. Written into a phase; the cost parameter stays null, because what is wrong is the reason given for the blank, not the blank.

### 4. One lookup, two prices

 The Developer Spec says one lookup is 8 tokens — 8p — and that is what the built connector spends: two for the postcode search, five for the address, one for the penny title pre-check. The source register row, the trial plan, and the Word questions document's worked example and its recommendation all say 7p, which was the design before the pre-check existed. The recommendation — buy a paid lookup only if a typed address fails often enough to cost more than 7p a property — is measured against the wrong number. Both figures are true of different things, which is why nothing caught it. Written into the same phase, with the instruction to decide sentence by sentence which of the two each one means.

### 5. A check that says it looked for a document and cannot see one

 The sign-off register check's fourth check prints "119 checked for an update, a file or a document" and its failure line reads "no update, no file and no document". Three of its four evidence columns have never been able to fire: **a document column returns an empty string in its text field even when a document is attached** — the document is in the value field — and the snapshot the check reads asks only for text. Proved on all six hub items. Nothing is wrongly passed today, because the only items carrying documents also carry updates. The defect is that the check asserts it did something it cannot do. Written into a phase, with the control that proves the arm can now fail.

### 6. Two API traps, both silent

 `items(ids: [...])` **returns only the first twenty-five items whatever the length of the array** — thirty-five in, twenty-five out, no error, no warning, and a `limit` argument does not lift it. This sweep lost forty-seven items' comments to it and found out only by counting what came back. And a `docs` query with six object identifiers returns an empty array, as COORDINATES already said — but **six single-identifier ****`docs`**** queries aliased into one call return all six**, which is now the cheapest way to verify the hub document identifiers. Both are in COORDINATES, and the second only after it had worked once.

### 7. Two comments the decisions had overtaken

 The analytics task's latest comment ended "There is no measurement id and no call site"; the phase that built the cookie choice on 22 September gave the ten measurement events their call sites and rewrote the check to assert it. And the phase for taking back a pick carried no update, no file and no document, so nothing on the board said what it was or what it waited for. Both now carry a correction. The analytics task stays parked, correctly: what it waits on is the website going live.

 Every buildable thing this sweep found is written into Phase 147 or Phase 148; everything that is not Claude's to decide is a written question under the person who must answer it. **The board carries no orphan**: re-derived at the close, the four items at "Ready — Claude can build" are Phase 146j, Phase 147, Phase 148 and the CIBSE plant lives, and each one is covered by a phase section in the action plan.

### Added at the close of the same sweep — an eighth finding, and it is a hole in the guard rather than a stale figure

 The sweep is told to read the drift checker's "no marker either way" section rather than trust its green line, and to **ask what phrasing it still cannot see**. Its classifier writes down two remaining blind spots of its own: a bare "N tests", and a marker hard-wrapped away from its figure inside a fence. Rather than repeat those, this sweep put ten candidate phrasings through the classifier with the four true totals as the live set. **One family of them is invisible, and it is the near neighbour of the blind spot closed on 10 September.**

 The pattern is one word. The classifier requires a figure to be immediately followed by its marker, so `1246 assertions pass` is seen and **`1246 engine assertions pass`**** is not** — not reviewed, invisible. So are "1246 site-harness assertions pass", "1246 back end tests pass", "All 1246 site-harness assertions pass" and "1246 of 1246 assertions pass". The fix of 10 September widened the expression to allow "assertions" or "tests" between the figure and the word "pass"; nothing was done about a word sitting before them. **"397 phase9 assertions pass" is the natural way to write it, and this corpus writes that way everywhere else.**

 **Nothing is escaping through it today.** Searched across the live documents, the Developer Spec, the guide, the file index and the snapshot: the shape does not currently appear anywhere, with a stale figure or a true one. So it is a gap in the guard, not a figure loose in the corpus — which is the distinction worth keeping, because the two need different urgency.

 **Where it now lives:** BUILDABLE — **added to Phase 148 in terms**, as point 5, with every probe line written out as a self-test case that must fail, the instruction to re-run the drift checker afterwards and read whatever the widening lights up rather than silencing it, and the reminder that the better fix is the one COORDINATES already names: a table of evidence should carry the command, not the number.

 **And the method is the finding as much as the result.** Four earlier sweeps reported this check's blind spots by quoting the comment inside it. A comment is a claim. Ten lines of probing found a sixth spot in a minute, and the same ten lines are now a control that will notice if the fix is incomplete.

## PHASE 151a — the land boundary wired to a site area, all of it switched off (24 September 2026, Opus, Mac copy, Lakhbir's MacBook Pro)

 **Run from the Mac copy. Commit bd9a573 on main, pushed.** Claimed on the action plan item at the start, cleared at the close. Every changed file has a `.bak-phase151a` sibling. **Run out of order, on Lakhbir's instruction:** his prompt was Phase 151a's, while Phase 146j stood first below COORDINATES. 146j is untouched and still first.

### DONE — with the evidence

-  **The council's file (point 1).** `09-app/backend/src/connectors/inspire-councils.ts` maps every ONS council code to HM Land Registry's file name. It is derived from the two published lists, never guessed: ONS's "Local Authority Districts (April 2025) Names and Codes in the UK" (the ONS Open Geography Portal's feature service, read 24 September 2026: 361 rows, 318 of them England and Wales, the same count as HM Land Registry's files; no 2026 list was on the portal) and HM Land Registry's 318 files. A rule pairs 310 by name alone (a prefix and suffix may be added around the ONS name, never a word changed). The eight left over are paired by hand with the reason: Hull, Rutland, Durham, the City of London, St Albans, Newcastle, North Yorkshire and King's Lynn. `tools/inspire-council-table.ts` rebuilds the table from a saved copy of the ONS list and refuses if anything is unpaired or paired twice; the copy read is kept outside git in `04-phase-work/phase151a/`. A council with no row is refused. **A site on a council boundary:** HM Land Registry puts a boundary polygon in both councils' files, so every council given is read; the same polygon in both is one polygon, two different polygons are refused, and the answer names the files read.

-  **The point (point 2).** A British National Grid easting and northing (entered by a person, or Homedata's own), or an ETRS89 latitude and longitude converted by Ordnance Survey's exact method, **OSTN15** (`src/connectors/ostn15.ts`: the National Grid projection on GRS80, then the 1 km grid's shifts by bilinear interpolation, as OS's guide publishes). The projection reproduces OS's own worked example to the millimetre (651409.903, 313177.270). Every doubt is refused, never approximated: no grid file (`CAPREBATE_OSTN15_FILE`, absent as shipped), a datum not stated as ETRS89, and a point outside the grid or next to a grid point OS marks as outside its area. `tools/ostn15-verify.ts` checks a real grid file against OS's own test points; no grid file was downloaded. **Found:** Homedata's published schema labels its latitude and longitude WGS84, not ETRS89, so they are refused (`HOMEDATA_COORDINATE_DATUM` is null). The same schema publishes `easting` and `northing`, so the address lookup now keeps them as a pair, inside the grid (`HOMEDATA_ADDRESS`, source register and name exclusion register), and they are the point. N4: no point, no lookup, and absent and "not sure" behave alike.

-  **The site area (point 3).** `siteAreaFromLandBoundary` in `src/connectors/site-area.ts` is the one back-end function, and the only file besides the fetcher that names `inspireBoundaryFetcher` (Phase 150's test now allows exactly this one caller, and fails if it ever writes the switch as true). It returns SWITCHED_OFF before anything else while `BOUNDARY_FETCHING_SWITCHED_ON` is false. Then it checks `checkBoundaryUse('INTERNAL_CALCULATION')`, checks the property is the company's, resolves the point and the councils, and keeps any site area already held. It injects the fetcher (one per council) into `fetchAndImportBoundary`, and stores `site_area_m2`, `site_area_m2_grade` (worst of the area's grade and the register's B) and `inspire_id` through the one door under `HMLR_INSPIRE`. It never throws for a lookup that did not work; every case is a state with a plain reason, and the area stays asked. The outcome and the stored record carry no polygon, map or coordinate; a test searches both for every coordinate of the polygon. **`HMLR_INSPIRE`**** had no entry in the name exclusion register, so the one door would have refused it:** it is subitem 15 now, keeping the area, its grade and the ID, and excluding names, proprietor, owner and title number. `councilOfPostcode` and `homedataPointOf` are the two inputs a caller will pass.

-  **One file a council a month (point 4).** `src/connectors/inspire-store.ts` keeps a council's `.zip` by council and release month (the month whose first Sunday has passed, HM Land Registry's publication day). A file is kept for no longer than the licence row's `cache_max_age_days` (35, read from the register, not restated), with its SHA-256 checked on every read. The folder is named by `CAPREBATE_INSPIRE_STORE_DIR`, and a folder inside the git working copy is refused before anything is created. The fetcher reads a kept file and only downloads on a miss, so two properties in one council make one download. `node src/cli.ts sweep-land-boundaries` deletes files nobody asked for again; a daily run of that line is all the host needs.

-  **Tests.** `test/phase151a.test.ts`, 33 tests, invented data only, no network. Proved red on the pre-change copy: in a worktree of the last commit, the whole file fails to load (its modules do not exist). With only the new modules added there, 8 fail: every test that stores (the old name exclusion register refuses the source), the one-download test (the old fetcher ignores the store) and Phase 150's old naming test. `caprebate-name-exclusion.test.ts` R1b is red on the old register.

-  **Documents.** The Developer Spec's INSPIRE row is rewritten, and its figures are re-derived. The land boundary item's attached document has a Phase 151a paragraph, re-attached and compared byte for byte. The name exclusion document has section A.12 and the Homedata widening, re-attached and compared. The name exclusion register item has two new subitems, 14 (Homedata, left unlisted since Phase 146d) and 15. FOR THE SOLICITOR, THE DPO AND THE DEVELOPER's SDP-P20 now says fifteen subitems and asks the officer to look at 14 and 15. The source register's SUPPLIER_DOCS for HMLR_INSPIRE records the ONS list and OS's guide. The plain-words check now reads the site area, council and OSTN15 files. Its two failing sentences were rewritten, and it is green.

-  **Checks, re-run at the close on the Mac copy:** `npm run check` 1458 pass / 0 fail across 73 files (lint:sql and typecheck clean); the site harness 1252 / 0 / 4 xfail in both modes; phase3 419; phase9 398, from inside their folders: 3,527 in all.  **Claimed at 14:26 BST (4c341c3) and cleared at the close.** Tracker row 13117648493, now Done. `.bak-phase146j` siblings of every changed file. **Nothing was switched on:** `PICK_SWITCHES.MATCH_REVIEW_PICK` and `CLAUDE_SWITCHES.DOCUMENT_READING` are still `false`, the free gate is shut, no key was added, and every test runs on recorded answers with no network. The two gates and N4 hold: an unanswered question, a `no`, a `not sure` and a withdrawn `yes` all keep nothing.

### DONE — with the evidence

-  **1 · Taking back a pick.** `takeBackPick` in `src/web/match-review.ts`, route `POST /staff/clients/{id}/research/pick/take-back`, a "Take this choice back" box on the lookup's own row that asks why — Phase 139's shape, not a second pick screen. It removes the **one** `register_records` row the pick wrote, found through `register_match_picks.record_id` and never re-derived from the key; puts the lookup back to FAILED, `MATCH_REVIEW`, so the list can be offered again, with the entry chosen before marked "taken back" and why; and **keeps the pick row** with who, when, why, the id of what it removed and what to look at again (migration 054: a partial unique index over the picks that stand, so the next pick on the same lookup cannot erase a take-back). Its own audit kind, `REGISTER_MATCH_TAKEN_BACK`, carrying the reason; the reason is screened the way the chain screens every detail, before anything is written. Only a login that can run the research, and only while the engagement is signed, asserted with the same function the pick uses. It does **not** need the pick switch: it shows no list and calls nothing, and a switch turned off must not lock a wrong choice in.
-  **The two things to get right.** (a) **Not a record another lookup wrote, and not one a person approved.** Found while building it: `takePick` recorded `record_id` by looking the entity up AFTER storing, so a pick of an entry already held from an earlier lookup named that older record as its own — and a take-back would have removed it. Migration 042's own comment always said `NULL` there. `takePick` now records only a record it wrote. A take-back is refused, in words, where the pick kept nothing of its own, where the record is older than the pick (a row written before this fix), and where any fact from the record's latest tick is APPROVED (Phase 139) — the tick comes off first. (b) **Not un-derived silently.** `src/web/take-back.ts` works out, from the rows, what was kept on the strength of the record while it stood: a site area worked out from Homedata's point, the check of who signed (Companies House, the care regulator — which does not ask again once it has an answer), a step the client was told was done, a report issued, a surveyor's job, and — for the funder's name — a grant recorded from a client document. Nothing is changed; the list is shown to the person, written on the lookup's line, kept on the pick row as kinds and counts, and read back onto the panel after the next run rewrites that line. What reads a register record LIVE (the checks panel, the missing-facts list, the register bundle `derive()` reads, the surveyor's payload, the CRM company name) changes the moment the record goes, so its questions are asked again.
-  **2(a) · Taking a yes back.** `withdrawVouch` in `src/web/documents.ts`, route `POST /staff/documents/{id}/vouch/withdraw`, "Take the yes back" on the document's page, asking why. It takes **that field and no other** out of every `CLIENT_DOC` record the yes let it into — one per reading of a version, found through the document's own versions — and keeps the answer, still `yes`, marked withdrawn with who, when and why; a withdrawn yes keeps nothing on the next reading. `DOCUMENT_FIELD_VOUCH_WITHDRAWN`, carrying the reason and never the name. Refused where the field itself is approved (an approval of another field does not block). The plain No button is refused once a yes has kept a name, and says to use the take-back; before anything was kept it still changes freely. The one door out is `removeRegisterRecord` and `removeRegisterField`, in `src/stubs/registers.ts` beside the one door in, and a test holds that no other file under `src/` deletes or rewrites a register record.
-  **2(b) · Asked before the first reading.** The question is on the staff upload forms (the client's files, the claim page), on the form where staff say what a file that came by email is, and on the document request. **One store:** an upload writes the same `document_field_vouches` row against the document it creates (`asked_on` UPLOAD); a request writes it against the request (`asked_on` REQUEST), and the **same row** is adopted by the document that answers it, inside the upload's transaction, before that document is read — found by the request named, or by the rule `receiveByUpload` uses, now one function (`openRequestFor`) so the answer adopted is always the request received. The page's answer governs: a document that already has one is neither written nor adopted over. Only the question the chosen type asks is kept; "Leave it for now" and an unknown value are no answer, never a no; a client's posted answer is ignored and never blocks their upload. The request's line shows the early answer.
-  **The tests.** `test/phase146j.test.ts`, twenty-nine. **Eleven deliberate breaks of the controls, each one at a time, were each caught by the test written for it** (J2, J6, J7, J8, J9, W1 with W4, W2, W5, E3 with E4, E5, E6), and the file was restored byte for byte after each. ## PHASE 151e, LINES 4 AND 5 — a check and its result on one database; the empty identity panel (27 September 2026, Opus, Mac copy, Lakhbir's MacBook Pro)

 **The prompt's two lines, restated on 27 September 2026.** Line 4: a check and its result on one database — the test website builds the application on a database in memory, so a result that reaches a copy of the website which did not send the check is refused. Line 5: on a client with no contacts the identity panel showed no form and said nothing (found by Lakhbir on 25 September 2026). Claimed (af1219a) under tracker row 13133268301; the claim is cleared. `.bak-phase151e3` siblings of every changed file (the plain `.bak-phase151e` copies belong to lines 1 to 3 and were not touched).

### DONE — with the evidence

-  **Read before choosing.** Vercel's documentation, read on 27 September 2026: a function has a read-only disk and a writable `/tmp` of up to 500 MB that is scratch space; lasting data means Blob (files), Global Config (settings) or a **Marketplace** database, each an account with its provider. The back end calls `db.run`, `db.get` and `db.all` and gets the answer at once, hundreds of times. **Turso** (SQLite, a native Marketplace integration) has a package, `libsql`, that answers the same way in the same SQL; a Postgres driver answers later and would change every call and 56 migrations. So the smallest true thing is `libsql` behind `src/db.ts`.
-  **(a) Built and switched off.** `src/db.ts`: a database knows where it is (`kind`: memory, file or remote — `libsql://` or `https://`; plain `http://` and a missing token refused) and which library answers (`engine`); the token is passed in by the caller, never read there. `api/index.mjs`: `lastingDatabase` uses the lasting database only when its address, its token (`TURSO_DATABASE_URL` and `TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN`, as Vercel's Turso integration names them, or `CAPREBATE_DB_URL` and `CAPREBATE_DB_TOKEN`, which win) **and** the test password are all set; `seedOnce` seeds only an empty database; a copy that could not start tries again on the next request; the outbox printer shows only what this copy's life added. `libsql` 0.5.29 is in both `package.json` files, as Phase 151e line 1's test requires. **It needs an account, so it is Lakhbir's**: Word question 230 under his name, the Developer Spec's one page (a Turso row) and a "Built by Phase 151e, lines 4 and 5" section, and the row is at Ready - Lakhbir action, owned by Lakhbir.
-  **The whole back end runs on libsql.** One run of every back-end test with every database opened through `libsql` (a scratch copy, with the default flipped): first 1568 of 1620, which found the two differences — libsql adds a `_metadata` field to each row and gives bytes as an `ArrayBuffer` — both now handled in `src/db.ts` (`asNodeSqliteRow`); then **1618 of 1620**, the two failures needing the `.bak` files and git that the scratch copy lacked, and failing the same way on `node:sqlite` there.
-  **(b) Saying so.** On a database in memory the identity panel shows **Records kept in memory**, what that means, and to send the check again if no result shows. A signed result that finds no check is **still refused** (404), audited with `database: "in memory"` and what to do, answered `refused. This server keeps its records in memory only. The check may have been sent from a copy that has forgotten it. Send the check again.` — never matched to the nearest. The words come from `db.kind`; a query string cannot add or remove them (tested). On a file or remote database, nothing is said.
-  **Line 5.** A client with no contacts: **Nobody to check yet.** "A check goes to a contact of this client. Add the person as a contact first, then come back here to send it." and **Add a contact**, linking to `/staff/clients/<id>#contacts`, where the form is. The guide's B53 (two new boxes and one refusal) and the Help page (rebuilt, `--check` green) say the same.
-  **Tests, `test/phase151e3.test.ts`** (run it to count them): SIGNED, INVENTED results posted to `/hooks/identity-check` on recorded answers with no network — two copies on ONE database file, the check sent from the first and the result taken by the second, a 200 and the row, on `node:sqlite` and on `libsql`; a result for a check never sent refused there, with no memory note; two copies on two memories — refused, audited with what to do, nothing written; a bad signature refused as before; the panel's words on memory only; the empty panel's words and link, over HTTP; the entry point's switch in every half-set combination; the seed once. **Proved red on the pre-change code** (the six changed files put back in a scratch copy, the new names imported by namespace so each test runs): 12 red, and the 4 green are guards of behaviour that was already right (a bad signature, the form with contacts, Sales sees no panel, and the row test, which is proved red instead against the current `db.ts` without the normalisation).

Extraction verifier and `extract --check` exit 0. The drift checker went red on the two figures in the Developer Spec the new tests moved, which were updated, and is green; its self-test exit 0 and its negative control (on its own line) exit 1. ## PHASE 151i — the test website's uploaded documents on a store every copy reaches, switched off; the audit log on a shared database (28 September 2026, Opus, Mac copy, Lakhbir's MacBook Pro)

 Claimed (8339360) under tracker row 13133268308, now at Ready - Lakhbir action, owned by Lakhbir: connecting a private Blob store is his Vercel account. The claim is cleared. `.bak-phase151i` siblings of every changed file.

### DONE — with the evidence

-  **Read before choosing (Vercel's docs, 28 Sep 2026, not memory).** Vercel Blob has **private stores**: every read and write needs a token, and an object's address "is not publicly accessible". The `@vercel/blob` SDK (2.3 or later for private) signs in by the project's OIDC token with `BLOB_STORE_ID`, or by `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN`; `get` gives null for a missing object, `head` throws `BlobNotFoundError`, `del` of a missing object is not an error, and a deleted object can sit in Blob's cache for up to a minute. Hobby: 1 GB, 10,000 simple and 2,000 advanced operations a month free, and it stops rather than charges past that.
-  **The port is asynchronous** (every `ObjectStore` method answers with a promise), so no caller changed. Callers also use four things of `FsObjectStore` itself, so the new store **is** an `FsObjectStore`: `SharedObjectStore` (`src/web/shared-objectstore.ts`) replaces only the four steps that say where bytes go, which `src/web/objectstore.ts` now names (`readBytes`, `writeBytes`, `copyBytes`, `removeProven`; the folder's behaviour unchanged). Sealed originals, the retained text, the proved deletion and the one-key upload link all stay in the base class.
-  **Private.** Every call `access: 'private'` (a public store refuses, so it fails closed), `application/octet-stream`, the shortest cache, reads that skip the cache; the address Blob answers with is thrown away; a document leaves only through the routes that authorise each request. **One upload link secret** for every copy, derived (HKDF-SHA256) from the lasting database's token: with a secret made fresh in each process, a link issued by one copy is refused by the next.
-  **Switched off.** `api/index.mjs`: `sharedDocumentStore` needs the lasting database **in use** and `BLOB_STORE_ID` or a token (`CAPREBATE_BLOB_TOKEN`, else `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN`); `openLasting` hands the store to the lasting database only, never to memory; `@vercel/blob` 2.8.0 (root and back end) is loaded only then. The log says which, never a token or an id.
-  **The audit log (line 4).** `AuditLog.append` read the last hash and then, in a second statement, the next number. Now one statement reads both, and a clash on `seq` is read again and retried; `Db.tx` begins `IMMEDIATE` (the write lock first), and a second handle on a file waits five seconds for it. What a hash covers is unchanged.
-  **Tests, `test/phase151i.test.ts`** (run it to count them), on a Blob store answering as the SDK's documentation says, no network: a document, its retained text and a sealed original written by one copy and read by another; **two copies of the website on one database file**, Sales uploading through one and Admin opening the kept original through the other (signed in on the first); nothing without a session or for Accounting, and no Blob address anywhere in the database's bytes; the switch in every position; the audit log in turn, interleaved two ways, across two processes, and `verify-audit`. **Eleven were red on the pre-change `objectstore.ts`, `server.ts`, `audit.ts`, `db.ts` and `api/index.mjs`** (a scratch copy with those five put back, the new file kept), each for its own reason: the chain forked (`broken_at: 3`), the number clashed and the request was lost, "database is locked", the second copy answered 500, the bytes went to the copy's own disk. The other six guard what did not change or what lives only in the new file. `test/phase151e3.test.ts`'s entry-point assertion follows the new shape (the settings read once into `lasting`).
-  **The checks, re-derived at the close:** `npm run check` exit 0 (1,701 pass, 0 fail, 90 files); the site harness the same in both modes, 1,273 pass, 0 fail, 4 xfail; phase3 439 and phase9 398 green; the drift checker exit 0, its total **3,811** after the Developer Spec's two figures were updated; its self-test green and its negative control exit 1; extraction verifier and `extract --check` exit 0; plain words and its self-test green; tracker, register and CRM fold checks green with their self-tests (the fold check after two §4 line numbers in `server.ts` moved); payload proof PASS.
-  **Word question 231, "Can the test website keep uploaded files in a private store on Vercel?"**, under Lakhbir, after 230 (question 230's answer, "set up Turso", covers the database only, and its own suggestion said a later phase would fix files). Written the Amendment 2 way into the Mac file at 10:54: the cloud item, copied down at 10:53, was byte for byte the document from before 230 (`.bak-phase151e3`), so nobody had typed there; the new body deep-copied 230's eight paragraphs, and only `word/document.xml` went back into the original zip (every other entry byte-identical, every old paragraph kept in order). ## PHASE 151m — recovery codes: ten one-use codes, so a person who loses their phone can still sign in (28 September 2026, Opus, Mac copy, Lakhbir's MacBook Pro)

Claimed 45ee047. Every file changed has a `.bak-phase151m` sibling (`CLAIM.md`'s and the tracker's were written from the commit before the claim, because the claim was made first). Invented people only; no network beyond a test's own server on 127.0.0.1. Lakhbir, 28 September 2026, Word question 232 (closed): yes to recovery codes.

**DONE**

-  **1. The codes** (`src/web/recovery-codes.ts`, new). Ten at a time; each ten characters from 32 with no look-alikes (A to Z without I and O, and 2 to 9, one case), as two groups of five: 50 bits. Kept only as a hash in `recovery_codes` (migration 059, new: user, hash, made, used; a trigger keeps a used code used). The hash is scrypt (N 16384, r 8, p 1, about 30 ms on the Mac) salted with the person's id: one hash per try, compared in constant time with each unused code. **Why scrypt and not the SHA-256 the step tokens use:** 50 bits is short enough that a stolen table could be tried offline against a fast hash; a token has 256. Never as text, never in a log line or an audit row, never emailed. Checked with `git check-ignore -v`: none of the three new files is ignored.
-  **2. When they are made.** Setting up a second step (`submitCode` at SETUP, staff and clients, first sign-in or from **Your second step**) throws away any old codes, makes ten, and passes them **once** on the answer: the website's answer is now the codes page (200, the session issued with it, one link on to where the redirect went: "I have saved them. Continue"), saying save or print them, each works once, they will not be shown again. **Make new recovery codes** on `/staff/two-factor` and `/portal/two-factor` (`makeNewRecoveryCodes`) does the same from the account; refused with no second step. The JSON API, on the same functions: the setting-up answer carries `recovery_codes`; `POST /api/account/recovery-codes` makes new ones. Audited `RECOVERY_CODES_MADE`: why, how many made, how many unused thrown away.
-  **3. Using one** (`submitRecoveryCode`), at the VERIFY step only. Website: "Use a recovery code instead" (`/login/step?use=recovery`) posting to `/login/step/recovery`. **API: its own route, `/api/login/step/recovery`**, not `/code`, so a six-digit code and a recovery code are never guessed apart; a VERIFY answer says `recovery_code: true`. It counts toward the same 5 wrong codes (`countTry`, now shared by both), is used once (taken only while unused, checked by the row count), is audited `RECOVERY_CODE_USED` with `left` and never the code, and emails the person (new kind `RECOVERY_CODE_USED`, no code in it, so **not** added to `blankSentSecrets`). The session's audit row says `second_factor: RECOVERY_CODE`. With 2 or fewer left, the page after sign-in is **Your second step**, which says so in red and offers new ones; the email says to make new ones soon. A person who set a step up before this phase has none, so their next sign-in lands there, telling them to make some.
-  **4. What clears them.** Setting up a new second step, the super user's **Reset second step** (`resetTwoFactor`) and a client turning theirs off (`removeOwnTwoFactor`) delete them; `TWO_FACTOR_REMOVED` counts them. A new temporary password does not.
-  **5. Words.** The step page's line names recovery codes first ("Lost your phone? Use one of your recovery codes. No codes left? Then ask your administrator to reset your second step." — a client is told to contact us; an email user reads "Cannot get to your email?"). The guide's Admin section (the second step, and the two buttons) and `B55` say what they are, where to keep them and what to do when they run out, at grade 7; `src/web/help-content.ts` rebuilt from the guide with `node tools/build-help.cjs`, `--check` clean.
-  **6. Tests.** `test/phase151m.test.ts` (run `cd 09-app/backend && node --test test/phase151m.test.ts` to count them): ten made and shown once; hashes only; one signs in once and never twice, typed in any case; an email user too; a wrong one counts toward the 5, both ways round; the email and audit row carry no code; the low-codes landing; not taken at SETUP or on the six-digit form; new ones void the old; the reset clears them and a temporary password does not; a new step clears them; a client end to end; the API's path and its 5; Help and the guide. **Proved red** on a scratchpad copy of the back end with the six changed source files put back from their `.bak-phase151m` siblings, migration 059 and `recovery-codes.ts` removed, and the guide from before: every one failed, on its assertions (one on "no such table"), none on an import. `test/phase151j.test.ts` (six places) and `test/phase151k.test.ts` (one) now expect the codes page after a second step is set up on the website, not a redirect; each says so.
-  **Developer Spec:** the website and API route tables (the step routes, the two-factor routes, a new `/api/account/recovery-codes` row), the 151j section's line on recovery codes, a new "Built by Phase 151m", §4's two figures, and three §4 line citations my edits moved (`outboxTransport` `:152`, `STUB_NOTICE` `:184`, `CASE_STAMPED` `:276`, each re-read from the code).

## Ad-hoc fix, 29 September 2026 — no second step for the invented logins on the test website, and why the authenticator step "times out" (Opus, Mac copy)

 Lakhbir: "check the 2FA and stop it for the @example.invalid emails — every time I go to click 2FA via authenticator app the session times out." Claimed 55afb9e.

-  **The cause, reproduced.** A sign-in step is a row in the database (`sign_in_steps`) with a cookie pointing at it. On one copy of the website, choosing the authenticator app reaches the set-up page (200). On two copies each on its own in-memory database, the same click answers 401 "That sign-in has timed out" — Lakhbir's words. The lasting database (`src/db.ts`) talks to Turso directly, with no local replica, so with Turso in use every copy sees the step at once. So the live test website is most likely still on memory: Word question 230 (not yet confirmed) is the thing to check. Sessions are in the database too, so on memory a login can also drop between pages.
-  **What changed.** A third policy, `STAFF_EXCEPT_INVENTED` (`src/auth.ts`, `isInventedLogin`: the whole domain `example.invalid`, any case): no second step for the invented seed logins; a temporary password is still asked to change; every other login unchanged. Set only by `api/index.mjs` (`TEST_WEBSITE_TWO_FACTOR`); the default stays STAFF, and a test fails if any file under `src/` sets it. The time-out page now adds, on a memory database, why a step can be lost (`stepGoneWhy`, `STEP_LOST_ON_MEMORY`).
-  **Proof.** `test/invented-logins.test.ts`, eight tests. With the one exemption line removed, exactly the two invented-login tests fail; with the page words removed, exactly the time-out test fails. `npm run check` exit 0, **1799 pass** (was 1791, 96 files); the plain-words test caught the first wording at grade 10.9 and it was shortened. The Phase 152 sign-up test failed at random on the old code too (1 in 6 alone) — the known flake, Phase 153a line 7. The CRM fold check (one moved reference, `STUBS` to `src/app.ts:132`), the drift checker (`--fast --expect 1279,439,403,1799`: Developer Spec §4 moved to 1,799 and 3,920), plain words, brand, tracker and register checks all exit 0; the payload proof PASS.
-  DONE: the exemption, the explanation, the tests, the records. NOT DONE: confirming the live site is on Turso — BLOCKED on Lakhbir looking (Word question 230); the flaky sign-up test — BUILDABLE — Phase 153a line 7.

## Ad-hoc, 30 September 2026 — video calls through Zoom: a meeting for each, the link sent, joined inside the site (Opus, Mac copy)

 Lakhbir: "with the video call link this should be sent automatically, and i feel zoom would be best for this as we can run it via our platform, is there a way to have zoom embeded on our back end so its done though there?" Yes: Zoom's Meeting SDK for the web runs a Zoom meeting inside our own pages, and its Server-to-Server API makes the meeting. Built on that (developers.zoom.us, read 30 Sep 2026; Web SDK 6.5.0, whose files on source.zoom.us were checked).

-  **A meeting for each video call** (`src/connectors/zoom.ts`, `src/web/video-calls.ts`, migration 062 `video_meetings`). Given a time (at the figure page, or later by staff), Zoom makes the meeting: the time, an hour, the waiting room, and the words "Cap Rebate call" — never the client's name, email or number. Moved (staff or the client's portal): the same meeting moves, so the link does not change. Cancelled or its time given back: Zoom deletes it and our row closes, so the link stops.
-  **The link goes out by itself**: the invitation (email and calendar file) carries OUR join page, `/call/<token>`, then Zoom's own link and passcode. It waits in the outbox like every email until email sending is switched on; meanwhile the thank-you page gives the client the join link at once.

## Ad-hoc, 1 October 2026 — why no email went out (Opus, Mac copy)

-  **Found, by signing in to IONOS and out again from the Mac with nothing sent:** (1) the key file names port 587, which starts in plain text and turns secure with STARTTLS; the adapter opened every port as 465, so IONOS hung up before its greeting ("wrong version number"); (2) `IONOS_SMTP_USER` names another mailbox — IONOS answers 535; the same password with `contact@caprebate.co.uk` (the IMAP user) answers 235.

Checked live on 587 with the right user: accepted. `test/smtp-starttls.test.ts`, two tests, three mutations red; `npm run check` 1916 pass (109 files); drift (`--expect 1279,439,403,1916`), fold (five §4 references moved), plain words, brand, register, analytics green.

 Lakhbir: "the email sent to icloud, i cloud responded but it didnt push through to back end" … "so no emails pull through … have a look and fix it". In order, each pushed and live: a reply from the very address our email went to is filed; replies to our emails are read wherever staff look (Email page, client page, Home) and a reply to one of ours is never skipped by the reading mark (`Mailbox.answering`, read-only `UID SEARCH HEADER IN-REPLY-TO`); a reply set aside before those rules is filed by them (migration 068, `rule` on a filing); the Everything tab shows emails to a typed address; "How email reading stands" on Email replies to sort.
-  **The root cause**, found through that panel and the deploy's build log (read in the browser pane, Lakhbir signed in to Vercel): every copy of the test website ran on its own memory — "the lasting database holds a seed that never finished" — because each deploy's refill of Turso stopped on `stream not found`. An email sent on one copy was unknown to the copy that read its reply; sign-ins did not last. Fixed in `src/db.ts` (`droppedConnection`: reopen and retry once; a dropped transaction begun again from the start; remote only). The next build: "the lasting database was left part built, so it was emptied, built and seeded". The test website started afresh (nothing anybody typed had ever been kept). Lakhbir then tested end to end: "yes its working".
-  **The reply timer** (Lakhbir chose option 2, a free outside timer): `GET · POST /hooks/read-replies` with `Authorization: Bearer <REPLY_TIMER_TOKEN>`; refused without the word (32+ characters, constant-time); reads at most every two minutes; counts only in the answer. `REPLY_TIMER_TOKEN` added to SECRET_KEYS, secrets.example.env and the test website's TEST_DEPLOY_KEYS.
-  **Proof.** `test/db-reconnect.test.ts` (4), `test/reply-reading.test.ts` (7), `test/conversations.test.ts` (8); every new guard broken on purpose and caught. `npm run check` 1926 pass (110 files); drift (`--expect 1279,439,403,1926`), CRM fold, plain words, brand, register and analytics green.
-  **For Lakhbir:** make the timer's word, add it to Vercel as REPLY_TIMER_TOKEN and redeploy, then set up cron-job.org to call the address every 5 minutes with the header.

## Faster clicks, 3 October 2026 (Claude Code, on the Mac)

 Lakhbir: "The back end is really slow to react to clicks, why is that?" — then "do it".

-  **Found:** on the test website every database query is a trip over the network to Turso, and a click asked hundreds (Home 467 to 737). Measured read-only in a browser: Home 4.6 s, Clients 2.1 s, Pipeline 1.1 s, Tasks 0.9 s; the same pages build in 0.01 to 0.03 s on the Mac.
-  **Built, part 1:** a click asks each question once (`withReadMemo`, src/db.ts); any write forgets at once, and nothing is remembered inside a transaction. Home 737 → 177 trips (Sales), 467 → 148 (Admin); Tasks 234 → 68.
-  **Built, part 2, switched off:** a local copy of the database on each copy of the website, brought up to date at the start of every click, when the website's settings say `CAPREBATE_DB_LOCAL_COPY=on`; if it cannot open, the website uses the database as before. Not yet proved on Turso (no libSQL server on the Mac); to be tried on the test website, with Lakhbir's go-ahead to add the setting.
-  **Proof.** `test/faster-clicks.test.ts`, ten tests; 19 single-line mutations, all red. A first full run was spoiled — the mutation run changed src/db.ts while the suite was running — so it was stopped and the whole suite run again. A second run had whole files fail with ETIMEDOUT reading the source: OneDrive stopped answering for a while; once it answered, the suite was run a third time. 2220 tests: all pass but the stray-file one (`whatsapp.test.ts` passed this time). `test/phase151i.test.ts`'s check that the shared document store goes only to the lasting database now reads the options named once, `remote`, and both ways of opening. Type check, CRM fold, plain words, analytics and drift (`--expect 1279,439,403,2220`) green.
-  **Next:** Lakhbir merges; then measure the test website again; then, with his go-ahead, switch the local copy on and measure.

 **Claim cleared** in the commit that carries this record.

## Faster clicks 2, 3 October 2026 (Claude Code, on the Mac)

### What Lakhbir asked, and the answers given in the chat

- What the flat 15% is for, since our fee is fixed at 3%: it is not our fee. It estimates the design-team fees (architects, engineers, quantity surveyors) the client paid on top of the build cost, whose plant share can be claimed too. It has no source (register R-B9); a competitor's report (the Eureka benchmark) uses the same 15% on top of BCIS element costs. Our 3% fee is unchanged.
- Whether BCIS gives ageing: mostly not. BCIS gives build costs and price indices; plant lives come free from CIBSE Guide M; how much value is lost by a given age is a valuation method, the surveyor's to choose.
- Whether the 15% would come from BCIS: no. BCIS costs are the builder's price; fees go on top as a rule of thumb.
- What the Valuation Office was for: nothing essential — a published source for the fee percentage and a ready-made ageing scale, both restricted to its own rating work. Then: "dont send it".

## PHASE 156b — DONE: email — the reply timer and signed emails (5 October 2026, Opus 5.5, Mac copy, Lakhbir's MacBook Pro)

**Run-sheet entry.** Phase 156b - 5 October 2026 - DONE. The reply timer works: cron-job.org (Lakhbir's account) calls the website to read client replies, every run 200 OK; Lakhbir moved it from every minute to every 5 minutes. Emails are signed: caprebate.co.uk publishes SPF (IONOS), DKIM (s1-ionos and s2-ionos) and DMARC (p=none), and a test email from the back office scored 10/10 on mail-tester.com, so there was nothing to fix in code. No code changed; figures 1363 / 440 / 415 / 2438 = 4,656. Branch claude/phase-156b.

### What was done and found

- **DNS, read from outside (dig):** TXT on caprebate.co.uk "v=spf1 include:_spf-eu.ionos.com ~all"; s1-ionos and s2-ionos._domainkey are CNAMEs to IONOS with DKIM keys; _dmarc "v=DMARC1; p=none;"; MX mx00 and mx01.ionos.co.uk. So A2's DNS part was already done.
- **The outgoing message (src/stubs/email-provider.ts), read:** From, Reply-To, To, Subject, Date, Message-ID on caprebate.co.uk, MIME-Version, plain text in base64; EHLO names caprebate.co.uk. Nothing a spam filter would mark down; mail-tester agreed (10/10).
- **The reply timer:** POST /hooks/read-replies without the word answers the website's own refusal ("no word was sent"), so Vercel's protection is not in the way. Lakhbir's cron-job.org history (screenshot, 5 Oct): every run "Successful, 200 OK", every minute; moved to every 5 minutes (1,440 IONOS logins a day were more than needed; Admin's warning fires after 60 minutes without a read). The longer runs (6 to 11 s) are the website starting from idle.
- **Not possible from here:** reading the mailbox_reads row or the Vercel logs (the connector's log access is refused, 403); the 200s in cron-job.org's history are the proof instead.

## PHASE 156c — DONE: WhatsApp by manual upload — a chat exported on the phone, added to the client's record (5 October 2026, Opus 5.5, Mac copy, Lakhbir's MacBook Pro)

**Run-sheet entry.** Phase 156c - 5 October 2026 - DONE. Staff can now add a WhatsApp chat exported on the phone (Export chat > Attach media) to a client's record: the WhatsApp page's "Add a WhatsApp chat", then a check (counts, dates, which name is us, keep from a date — an export holds the whole history), then save. Photos, videos, voice notes, PDFs and Office files come with it; a big export is opened on the staff member's computer and only the chosen period's files are sent. A newer copy adds only what is new; group chats are refused; imported messages never show as unread. With the live connection off, the WhatsApp page has no reply box ("reply on the phone"). Checked privately against a real iPhone export: 40 test messages and 4 files from 5 October, nothing earlier. Back end 2464 pass / 0 fail; figures 1363 / 440 / 415 / 2464 = 4,682. Branch claude/phase-156c.

### Lakhbir's part, and the real export

- **A1:** an iPhone export ("WhatsApp Chat - Zara.zip", 53 MB) — a real chat used with the other person's consent, holding the WHOLE history (84 days, about 10,000 lines, 206 files including a contact card and a Word document), because WhatsApp's Export chat always does. Only its 5 October lines were read, for the layout, with every word masked; earlier lines were counted by date only. The folder 09-app/backend/test/fixtures/whatsapp-export/ is git-ignored (.gitignore); the tests build invented exports. No Android export: built from WhatsApp's documented layout, tested on invented files (WAITING-ON-PEOPLE asks for one).
- **A2:** answered by Lakhbir 5 Oct 2026 — the copies follow the client-message retention rule ("yes same rules"); messages from before the client ticked the WhatsApp box are kept ("kept in"). Recorded for Sadique to confirm (FOR-THE-SOLICITOR-DPO-DEVELOPER; WAITING-ON-PEOPLE).

### What was found on the way

- **The layout's quirks** (iPhone): CRLF between messages and a bare LF inside one; U+200E before file lines and WhatsApp's own words; a document as "name • 1 page <attached: …>"; "You deleted this message." vs "This message was deleted."; " <This message was edited>"; an empty message.
- **A notice filter too broad:** a first "… added …" notice pattern swallowed 212 view-once notices ("For added privacy…") in the real file. Narrowed to WhatsApp's true notices; a view-once is shown as "A view-once message — WhatsApp does not put these in an export."
- **The test website takes about 4.5 MB a request** (Vercel), against a 53 MB export. Hence the page's script: it opens a .zip over 3.5 MB on the person's computer, sends only the chat's text and the file names, and after saving only the files still needed from the dates kept, one at a time (each under 4.4 MB; a bigger one is added by hand). The file is remembered in the browser (IndexedDB) between the two pages; without it, the person chooses the .zip again.

### What was built

- **Reader** src/connectors/whatsapp-export.ts (`parseChat`): both layouts, 12-hour times, day first with a month-first warning, UK time to an exact moment across the clock change.
- **Steps** src/web/whatsapp-import.ts and src/web/whatsapp-import-pages.ts; migration 090 (`whatsapp_imports`, `whatsapp_import_lines`): upload (whole up to 100 MB, kept sealed under the new `whatsapp-imports/` prefix in src/web/objectstore.ts; or text + names); refusals (not a chat, no chat in the .zip, a name that climbs out, a .zip inside, a group chat, a contact not of this company); check; save (IN RECEIVED / OUT SENT by the uploader, the message's own time, a fingerprint so nothing is saved twice); files from the kept .zip or one at a time, each sealed as a WhatsApp file (`whatsapp_media`, media id `export:<name>`); cancel. `listZipEntries` added to src/web/zip.ts (the one zip reader). Audit kinds WHATSAPP_EXPORT_UPLOADED and WHATSAPP_EXPORT_SAVED (counts only).
- **The page** src/web/whatsapp-page.ts: "Add a WhatsApp chat" with how to export; the uploads list; imported lines marked "From the phone", our side "<name> (on the phone)"; with the live connection off, no reply box and no opening message; its own policy (script-src 'self'; connect-src 'self') and /assets/whatsapp-import.js (src/web/whatsapp-import-script.ts, no innerHTML; calls through `root.fetch` like the other page scripts). Imported messages are left out of the unread count and never open the 24-hour window (src/web/messages.ts, src/web/whatsapp.ts).
- **Tests:** test/phase156c.test.ts, twenty-six (red on main: the modules do not exist there), including the script run in a stand-in browser (node:vm with Node's Blob, File, FormData and DecompressionStream). test/whatsapp.test.ts and test/conversations.test.ts restated for the page without a reply box.
- **Paper:** the Developer Spec (a Phase 156c note; figures), KEYS-AND-SWITCHES (WhatsApp row), WAITING-ON-PEOPLE (Sadique's confirmation; an Android export), ACTION-PLAN (the DECIDED entry; the phase removed), the run sheet. The notices page does not mention WhatsApp, so nothing there changed.

- ~~The Communication tab's one form still lists WhatsApp as a way to write~~ — done the same day (below).

A private demo on the Mac (invented company and chat, in memory, deleted after) showed the WhatsApp page and the company's conversation; the screenshots went to Lakhbir.
