## Phase 156f — Homedata as the property source: one address box, a daily cap, planning after signing, the site boundary — 6 October 2026 (Claude Code, on the Mac)

**Actions and outcomes (the same short entry is at the end of the run sheet).** The assessment's "Find my address" now uses Homedata: the person types a postcode, the list fills once it is complete (2p), narrows in the browser as they type, hides what is not a building, and the address they pick carries its UPRN onto their record. GoAddress is removed. The box is capped at £1 a day (50 searches, 5 per visitor). After signing, the paid research starts from that UPRN (if it belongs to the address given), Homedata answers planning history in place of the free route, and the site area is worked out from Homedata's title outline and kept as one number, for our own checks only. A real bug was found and fixed on the way: the title pre-check had said "no registered title" for every property. Two logged test lookups on 10 Downing Street (18p) gave real answers as fixtures. Tests: back end 2,525, all green; total 4,743. Branch `claude/phase-156f`, pull request against main.

Lakhbir's decisions, 6 Oct 2026, in the chat that planned this phase: "one address box on Homedata, with GoAddress removed - yes"; the £1 a day cap, "yes please"; "planning history - use homedata"; "site boundary - use home data"; listed buildings, "dont built this"; a street-name type-ahead not built (postcode route only). PART A (his) was done before the phase: a card on the Homedata account and `HOMEDATA_API_KEY` in Vercel and the key file.

- **B1, the address box** (`src/connectors/address-lookup.ts`, rewritten). `GET https://api.homedata.co.uk/address/postcode/{postcode}/` with `authorization: Api-Key`, the postcode and nothing else, through a new outside-call row `HOMEDATA_POSTCODE` (UK, 2p, Homedata's bucket; not a register lookup, so nothing from it is stored as a register fact). `readAddresses` reads the live shape (uprn, address, building_name, building_number, sub_building, street, town). `NOT_A_BUILDING` is a tested list: advertising rights (ADSHEL, "advertising right"), vessels, houseboats and lines starting with a berth or mooring (not "12 The Moorings", a street of houses), development sites, telephone masts and substations, parking spaces, "land at/adjacent", street records. "My address is not in the list" is always offered. The page (`src/web/funnel4.ts`, `src/web/router.ts`): the picker sits in a `.f4-addr` box; `POST /assessment/details/addresses` answers the page's one script (`src/web/address-lookup-script.ts`, `/assets/address-lookup.js`, `root.fetch`, `textContent` only) with JSON; the details page alone gets `script-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'` (`ADDRESS_PAGE_CSP`), nothing else loosened; with no script the "Find my address" button still works. A postcode already searched in the same assessment is never searched again. The pick sets `uprn` on the building; `submit` now writes each building's postcode, street, town and UPRN onto its property (migration 092: `properties.uprn`). **GoAddress removed**: its connector code, `GOADDRESS` call row, `GOADDRESS_API_KEY` (secrets.ts, secrets.example.env, `TEST_DEPLOY_KEYS`), its saved-key case, its Connections row and its tests; the Homedata key's "in use" now also counts the address box. Why: Lakhbir's decision; GoAddress gave no UPRN and listed one hospital five times, its 100 free lookups were used and its paid plan was never wanted.
- **B1, the research step** (`src/connectors/homedata.ts`). With a UPRN on the property, the paid address lookup first asks `/property/{uprn}/` and keeps it only if its own postcode and address match what the client gave (`uprnBelongs`, the EPC threshold, accept only); a mismatch falls back to the postcode search, and the property already read is not asked for twice. `runOrder` now runs the postcode table, then the paid address lookup and the boundary, then the free lookups, so a click after signing hands the UPRN to the energy certificates and to Homedata planning.
- **A bug the first real answer showed.** `preCheckOf` read `title_number`; Homedata sends `title_no` and a `title_class` ("Absolute freehold title"). So the penny pre-check said "no registered title" for every property, including 10 Downing Street. Fixed and tested (both names read; freehold or leasehold from the class).
- **B2, the cap.** `ADDRESS_SEARCH_CAP` (50 a day, 5 a visitor, 2p) in one place; `searchesToday` counts the audit log's CONNECTOR_CALLED rows for `HOMEDATA_POSTCODE` since UK midnight, leaving out refusals; the visitor's count is on the draft. Past either: "We cannot look up more addresses just now. Please type your address below." and no call. The Connections page's Homedata row shows "Address box today: N of 50 searches (2p each)."
- **B3, planning.** `HOMEDATA_PLANNING` moved from `PAID_NOT_CHOSEN` (now empty) into `PAID_CONNECTORS` and onto `TEST_WEBSITE_PAID_LOOKUPS`. It is not a row of its own: in `consultAllowed` the PLANNING row is answered by Homedata when the letter is signed, its switch is on and the address lookup found the UPRN on this click; otherwise the free route answers as before. `research_sources.route` (migration 092) records `HOMEDATA_PLANNING`; a PLANNING row the free route answered before signing is asked again once (`homedataPlanningDue`). Homedata's records carry their own entity ids (`homedata:<reference>`), and once Homedata has answered, the facts list and the surveyor's view leave the free route's planning records out (`preferHomedataPlanning`, `supersededPlanning`): kept, not shown. One logged 5p lookup showed the real shape, and the reader now takes `proposal` for the description and leaves out an application flagged `postcode_matches_property: false`. `PLANNING_ROUTE` and the Connections row say it in words.
- **B4, the site boundary** (`src/connectors/title-boundary.ts`). The `title_boundary` slug (5p) is asked on the address lookup's own property call when `HOMEDATA_BOUNDARY` is on (a new switch, off; on for the test website). `titleBoundaryArea` reads the GeoJSON (a `{title_no, geometry: Polygon}` in longitude and latitude, read live), puts it on the National Grid's projection without the OSTN15 shifts (they move a site, they do not change its area) and measures it with the boundary module's own `parseBoundaryGeometry` and `computeSiteArea`: 10 Downing Street's title is 9,607.2 m² on the grid, against 9,610.8 m² on the ground by a second method (the 0.04% gap is the grid's scale factor, the same basis as INSPIRE). A zero-call `HOMEDATA_BOUNDARY` lookup keeps the area, its grade (B) and the UPRN under its own source, labelled "from the Land Registry title outline, via Homedata"; never the outline or the title number. New source register entry `HOMEDATA_BOUNDARY` (licence `HOMEDATA_TERMS`, every report channel shut) and name exclusion entry, subitem 18 (the one door refused it until then); the research panel's site area line shows it where no INSPIRE area is held. **Homedata's terms, read 6 Oct 2026**: section 4 bars passing on "our data without authorisation"; section 7 gives a limited licence; nothing on title outlines or reports. So internal only, and **Word question 245** asks Lakhbir to get Homedata's yes in writing (wording given).
- **B5, not built, on purpose**: listed buildings and conservation areas; a street-name type-ahead; GoAddress. All in ACTION-PLAN's DECIDED - DO NOT REOPEN.
- **The live lookups** (Word question 170's five conditions; the log outside the repository): `HOMEDATA_ADDRESS` 2 of 3 (10 Downing Street, SW1A 2AA: 2p postcode search + 11p property with address, lr_title and title_boundary), then `HOMEDATA_PLANNING` switched on in the log and 1 of 3 (5p). New smoke options `--save-answers <folder outside the repository>` (refused inside it) and `--uprn`. Fixtures in `09-app/backend/test/fixtures/phase156f/` (public values; Homedata's opaque `uprn_token` removed).
- **Tests.** `test/phase156f.test.ts`, twenty-one tests, including a whole "Run the research" click for a signed seeded client on the test website (address from the UPRN, boundary, Homedata planning, PlanIt not asked, the free route's record hidden, the site area line). Proved able to fail: with the pre-check fix and the UPRN step undone, five tests go red; with the pre-phase `research.ts`, two. Restated: `funnel4` (the box, on Homedata's shape), `phase146b` (GoAddress off the approved transfers), `phase146d`, `phase146g`, `phase151e`, `phase153b`, `phase153c`, `phase156e`, `dashboard-home`, `survey-stage6`; phase3's `caprebate-name-exclusion.test.ts` (R1, R1b) and `caprebate-source-register.test.ts` (T28).
- **The checks, re-derived.** Site harness 1,363 pass / 0 fail / 3 xfail; phase3 440; phase9 415; back end 2,525 pass / 0 fail over 155 tracked files; total 4,743. The plain-words check found three sentences above grade 9, rewritten. The CRM fold check found 22 moved Developer Spec line references (four of them, in `registers.ts`, were already stale on main after PR 27) and they were corrected; green. Tracker check green; register check OK; extraction unchanged.
- **Documents.** The Developer Spec (the address box row rewritten, a planning-and-boundary row, the figures); KEYS-AND-SWITCHES; WAITING-ON-PEOPLE; FOR THE SOLICITOR, THE DPO AND THE DEVELOPER (SDP-P6: GoAddress removed, the UPRN and the site area); the source register's Homedata findings (the real shapes) and HOMEDATA_TERMS (the terms read); the name exclusion document's draft A.15 (on disk, 08-monday-doc-exports). **Word, the AMENDMENT 2 way**, all three documents proved in the cloud byte for byte, pre-write copies equal to the Mac files, no conflict copies, temporary copies to the recycle bin: 202 (planning) answered with Lakhbir's words and moved to the closed document; 244 (approve GoAddress) closed as no longer needed; 245 added for Lakhbir; the Unanswered document carries 202 in its appendix and 245 in Lakhbir's section; QUESTIONS-WORD-HEADINGS.txt rebuilt.
- **Board and tracker.** This phase's item Done (group Z). The Homedata account item (12830173693) Done with its evidence; the Homedata licence item (13003875907) noted with question 245. The build queue was empty: no orphans.

## Phase 157c — what the Friary House run found: sending the letter, a DocuSign-style signature, and fifteen fixes — 6 October 2026 (Claude Code, on the Mac's OneDrive copy)

**Actions and outcomes (the same short entry is at the end of the run sheet).** Built sending the engagement letter from the client page (who and when, the client emailed, the first time they open it kept) and a DocuSign-style signature: drawn in a box or the typed name adopted, the record's fingerprint covering the drawing, a certificate of completion at the end of the signed PDF, and the signed copy downloadable by the client and by staff. Signing stays OFF. Fixed fifteen of the Friary House findings. The classifier refused, twice, a local override letting the simulation sign the TEST letter, so the run still stops at signing on Claude's side. 4,825 passing.

- **Claim.** hub/CLAIM.md and the tracker row 13217233117 (board and tracker: Working on it, this machine), pushed before work began. Branch `claude/phase-157c` from main after PR 30 merged.
- **Where it came from.** The end-to-end simulation of an invented client, Friary House Surgery, Plymouth (`04-phase-work/sim-2026-10-06/Friary-House-simulation-findings.md`, OneDrive; findings F1 to F21). It reached the engagement letter and stopped: nothing prepared or sent one (F21), and it could not be signed (F10). Lakhbir said yes to the phase and asked: "cant it be a docusign style document which captures a signed digital copy?"
- **Sending the letter (F21).** `src/web/engagement-send.ts`: `POST /staff/clients/{id}/engagement/send` (`engagement.send`, Admin and Sales; Read only refused). Raises the engagement if there is none, marks it SENT with `sent_at` and `sent_by`, audits `ENGAGEMENT_LETTER_SENT` (no address in it), and emails every client login the portal link through the outbox. Again: re-sends, the first sent time kept. Refused when signed, or with no client login. The client page has an "Engagement letter" section on the Files tab with each step and its time. `markViewed` keeps the first opened time.
- **The signature.** `src/web/signing.ts`, `src/web/signature-pad-script.ts`, `src/web/pdf.ts`. Drawn (strokes 0 to 1000, `parseInk`, `INK_LIMITS`; a tap is "too small") or adopted (the typed-name tick); neither is refused. A version 2 record binds the method, every stroke, the login's email and the letter's prepared, sent and opened times into its fingerprint; version 1 records are checked as before. The PDF draws the strokes and ends with a certificate of completion. Signed copy at `/portal/letter/signed.pdf` and `/staff/clients/{id}/engagement/signed.pdf`, checked against the record first. The pad and its one script appear only while the letter can be signed; as shipped, the page carries no script and every page's policy. **Migration 096**, ADD COLUMN only.
